View code echoes `$player->status_localised` + `$player->preferred_foot_localised` rather than calling `LabelTranslator::playerStatus( $player->status )` / `LookupTranslator::byTypeAndName('foot_options', $player->preferred_foot)` inline; bypass impossible at the view layer for any future site that goes through the repository fetch. **New `Infrastructure\Players\PlayersRepository`.** One read method this slice: `find( int $id )` returns the active (non-archived) player row hydrated with `status_localised` (via `LabelTranslator::playerStatus`) and `preferred_foot_localised` (via `LookupTranslator::byTypeAndName`). The hydration tries the canonical seeded slug `foot_options` first, falls back to the historic singular `foot_option` slug that one legacy callsite used (FrontendMyProfileView line 108 pre-refactor) — operators with either seed shape get the right Dutch label. Raw `status` + `preferred_foot` stay on the row for back-compat (KPI joins, filter dropdowns, JSON exports). **`FrontendPlayersManageView::loadPlayer` refactor.** The view's private fetch helper now delegates to `PlayersRepository::find()`; inline SQL + per-row LabelTranslator/LookupTranslator calls remain in the existing view render code where they were — same module-by-module discipline as #1077 / #1078. New consumers that go through `loadPlayer` get pre-localised fields by construction. **Position labels deliberately not hydrated.** `preferred_positions` is a JSON array on `tt_players`; per-element translation belongs to a helper, not a row-level field. Same scoping discipline as the previous slices that left adjacent translation paths untouched. **What this is NOT.** Not a sweep of every Players callsite (FrontendPlayerDetailView's hero pill, REST list endpoint, FrontendMyProfileView's Playing details card, exporters) — those keep their existing inline translation calls until each is touched separately. CI lint allow-list tightens for Players once those land. **Refs remaining slice.** #1080 (Pdp) — last in the #806 series. Patch bump. (closes #1079) =

= 4.20.18 — Architecture: LookupTranslator into Goals repository — module-by-module rollout (closes #1077; refs #806 / #1078-1080). Second slice after #1081 shipped the Evaluations module under v4.17.2. Same shape: view code echoes `$row->status_localised` / `$row->priority_localised` instead of calling `LabelTranslator::goalStatus( $row->status )` inline, so bypass becomes structurally impossible at the view layer. **Mechanical difference vs. #1081.** Evaluations had a FK to `tt_lookups` so the precedent hydrated via `LookupTranslator::name()` after pulling the full lookup row. Goals store `status` + `priority` as code strings directly on `tt_goals` (no FK), so the per-row hydration calls the existing `LabelTranslator::goalStatus()` / `LabelTranslator::goalPriority()` switches. The contract is identical — repository returns pre-localised fields — only the lookup mechanism differs. **New `Infrastructure\Goals\GoalsRepository`.** Two read methods: `listForPlayer( int $player_id )` returns the player's active goals newest-first; `findForPlayer( int $goal_id, int $player_id )` returns a single goal scoped to that player (or null — replaces the inline SQL that let URL-tweakers drill into other players' goals via a stale id with no scope guard beyond the join column). Both methods filter by `CurrentClub::id()` so a future multi-tenant install can't leak goals across academies. Both run rows through a private `hydrate()` helper that adds `status_localised` + `priority_localised` while keeping the raw fields for back-compat (KPI groupings + filter dropdowns key off the canonical codes). **`FrontendMyGoalsView` refactor.** Both render paths (list at `?tt_view=my-goals` and detail at `?tt_view=my-goals&id=N`) route through the repository. Inline `wpdb->get_results` + `LabelTranslator::goalStatus($g->status)` calls in the loop are gone; the view echoes `$g->status_localised` directly. **REST controller** `GoalsRestController::format_row` adds `status_localised` + `priority_localised` keys alongside the existing `status` / `priority` raw codes (mirrors the EvaluationsRestController shape from #1081). Existing consumers that key off raw codes are unaffected; new consumers get the right string without re-implementing the LabelTranslator switch. **What this is NOT.** Not a sweep of every Goals callsite — same module-by-module pattern as #1081, which only refactored `FrontendMyEvaluationsView` + the REST controller. Other Goals consumers (FrontendGoalsManageView, FrontendPlayerDetailView's goals tab, CoachForms, exporters, KPI sources) continue to use `LabelTranslator` directly until each is touched for its own reason. Per the parent #806's plan, the CI lint allow-list tightens for Goals once the rest of those callsites land. **Refs remaining slices.** #1078 (Activities), #1079 (Players), #1080 (Pdp). Patch bump within v4.20 series. (closes #1077) =

= 4.20.17 — Academy admin can view + complete workflow tasks assigned to others (closes #1152). Pilot 2026-06-03 ask: when a coach is ill or unresponsive and a workflow task they own is blocking the rest of the chain, the academy admin needs a way to step in and complete the task on their behalf. **Three layers cooperated to block this:** academy_admin's matrix held `workflow_tasks` + `task_completion` at `self` scope (admin sees + acts only on their own); no cap was bridged from `task_completion:create` so per-cap checks had nothing to test; [FrontendTaskDetailView.php:84](src/Modules/Workflow/Frontend/FrontendTaskDetailView.php#L84) hard-gated submission on `$is_assignee` so non-assignee POSTs were silently dropped. **Matrix change.** `academy_admin` now holds `workflow_tasks => [r, global]` + `task_completion => [rc, global]` in [config/authorization_seed.php:657-660](config/authorization_seed.php#L657-L660). Other personas (HC, AC, parent, scout, observer, etc.) stay `self` — the takeover affordance is admin-only. **Backfill migration 0147** (`0147_academy_admin_workflow_global_scope.php`) runs the same conservative pattern as 0136: only flips `is_default = 1` rows so operator-customised overrides via the Authorization admin keep their scope; idempotent re-run safe. Flushes the matrix cache after the change so admin sessions in flight pick up the new shape without a forced refresh. **Detail view relaxation.** Replaced the `$is_assignee` gate with a `$can_submit = $is_assignee || $can_takeover` derived from `MatrixGate::can( $user_id, 'task_completion', 'create', MatrixGate::SCOPE_GLOBAL )`. Going through `MatrixGate` rather than a `LegacyCapMapper` bridge because the legacy bridge resolves via `canAnyScope` — that would let a coach with `task_completion [rc, self]` through too, defeating the takeover gate. When the viewer holds takeover, an amber "Completing on behalf of [Name] — this action will be recorded in the audit log" banner replaces the normal "view-only" notice, and the submit button label switches to "Complete on behalf" so the operator is visually aware they're acting as a stand-in. **Audit log entry** `workflow.task.completed_on_behalf` carries `task_id`, `template_key`, `assignee_user_id`, `completed_by_user_id` so the takeover trail is queryable post-hoc. Only fires when completer ≠ assignee. **Backward compatibility.** Existing assignee-only flows render identically; non-assignee non-admin viewers still see the read-only view-only banner. **Dutch translation** added for the two new strings. **Out of scope.** Per-task reassignment (admin changes the assignee instead of completing); HoD takeover; bulk completion from the dashboard kanban. Single-task admin takeover unblocks the immediate operational case. Patch bump. (closes #1152) =

= 4.20.15 — Activity ↔ principle link table: missing rename migration shipped + `PrincipleLinksRepository` write failures now log loudly (closes #1153). Pilot 2026-06-03 reported that ticking principles on the new-activity wizard's #1122 picker appeared to save but produced an empty pre-fill on the activity edit form. **Root cause.** Migration 0015 created the pivot as `tt_session_principles` with a `session_id` column. Migration 0027 (sessions → activities rename) renamed `tt_sessions`, `tt_attendance.session_id`, the caps, and the workflow triggers — but **did not rename the link table** to its activities counterpart. Yet every consumer (the new-activity wizard's PrinciplesStep, the wp-admin Activities form, the REST controller's `persistPrincipleLinks`, the frontend edit form's pre-fill, the planner's #1124 principle pills, the activity detail's #1037 linked-principles section, [PrincipleLinksRepository::sessionPivot()](src/Modules/Methodology/Repositories/PrincipleLinksRepository.php#L28-L31)) targets `tt_activity_principles` with an `activity_id` column. Result: every write returned `false` (silently swallowed by the repository); every read returned an empty array (table-not-found). Symptom-equivalent silent failure to #1054 and #1137. **Migration 0146** runs the missing rename: `RENAME TABLE tt_session_principles → tt_activity_principles`, then `ALTER TABLE CHANGE session_id activity_id`, then index renames (`uniq_session_principle → uniq_activity_principle`, `idx_session → idx_activity`). Idempotent + conservative — each step gates on current state; a fresh install lacking both names recreates the table at the new name via `dbDelta`. **Repository hardening.** `setActivityPrinciples()` now logs `principle_links.delete.failed` + `principle_links.insert.failed` with `$wpdb->last_error` + the offending ids when either call returns `false`. Future regressions surface in the error log instead of going silent. **What this resolves downstream.** #1037 (activity detail not rendering linked principles) and #1124 (planner principle pills) are both consumers of the same broken pivot; they begin working as soon as the table rename completes. **What it does NOT resolve.** Selections that operators made BEFORE this migration shipped were never persisted — those clicks have no recoverable state. = 4.20.12 — Print doelenintake: scope-mismatch fix on the player + team batch print routers (closes #1149). Pilot 2026-06-03 clicked "Print doelenintake" on a player profile that renders fine, hit a hard `wp_die( 'Player not found.' )` on the print URL. **Root cause.** [PlayerGoalIntakePrintRouter::emit](src/Modules/Goals/Print/PlayerGoalIntakePrintRouter.php#L161-L179) filtered the player lookup by `pl.club_id = CurrentClub::id()` (always `1` today), while the player profile view at [FrontendPlayersManageView::loadPlayer](src/Shared/Frontend/FrontendPlayersManageView.php#L631-L640) does NOT filter on club_id — only demo-scope. Same scope-strictness family as #1054 (silent `$wpdb->update`) and #1137 (archive REST). **Fix.** Two queries change: per-player `emit()` and the team-batch `renderTeamBatch()`. Both drop the `pl.club_id = %d` / `t.club_id = %d` filter, switch to `QueryHelpers::apply_demo_scope` (the same helper the linking surface uses), and derive `$club_id` from the player's own row to drive the downstream `lastSeasonStats()` + `lookbackForPlayer()` sub-queries. Net effect: the print router stops being a stricter gate than the page that linked here; demo-mode isolation is preserved (a demo user still sees only demo rows). **What this is NOT.** Not a `tt_players.club_id` data backfill — that's a separate hygiene task. Not a change to MatchPrepPrintRouter, which has the identical shape (file follow-up if pilot surfaces it). Patch bump. (closes #1149) =

= 4.20.9 — Authorization matrix admin: suppress spurious "Nog geen tegel of admin-pagina gebruikt deze entiteit" notice on 10 legitimately admin-only entities (closes #1159). Pilot reported that the Authorization Matrix admin page rendered the orphan-entity warning on a large number of rows — 10+ entities — even though every flagged entity is correctly wired (just to admin / configuration surfaces rather than frontend tiles). The notice was supposed to flag genuinely orphan entities (seeded in the matrix but never wired to any UI surface), but the detection logic produced false negatives for admin-only surfaces that lack a clean cap→entity mapping. **Root cause.** `MatrixEntityCatalog::consumersOf()` walks three registries (`TileRegistry` + `AdminMenuRegistry` + `AdminMenuRegistry::allDashboardTiles()`) looking for entries whose `cap` maps (via `LegacyCapMapper::capsForEntity()`) to the entity. Detection returned empty for each, MatrixPage rendered the warning, the operator saw a wall of "this entity is orphan" notices on entities that are actually fine. **Fix.** New `ADMIN_ONLY_ENTITIES` const list in `MatrixEntityCatalog` enumerating the 10 entities that legitimately live in admin surfaces. New private `adminOnlyDescriptor( $entity )` returns a synthetic consumer descriptor `{ type: 'admin_only', label: 'Admin / configuration surface' }` when the entity is whitelisted; returns empty array when not (preserving the genuine "no consumers" signal for true orphans). `consumersOf()` falls through to `adminOnlyDescriptor()` in two branches: when `capsForEntity()` returns empty (no cap mapping at all) AND after the dedupe pass when the walk found nothing. `MatrixPage::renderConsumerChip()` extended with the new `'admin_only'` type → "admin / configuration surface" label. **Operator UX.** The 10 whitelisted entities now show a single "Admin / configuration surface" chip in the consumer column instead of the red orphan warning. The chip's popover surfaces the entity name for traceability. **Adding entities to the whitelist** is a deliberate declaration: "this entity is intentionally only consumed by admin surfaces, not by the frontend tile registry." Frontend-tile-bearing entities should NOT be added — they should declare their entity on the tile. **What this is NOT.** Not a permission change — the matrix still gates these entities exactly as before via caps. Not a data change. Just a discovery-side false-positive fix in the admin tool. Patch bump. (closes #1159) =

= 4.20.7 — PlayerSearchPicker: dispatch synthetic `change` event after JS-driven value assignment (closes #1157). Pilot reported that on any wizard step using `PlayerSearchPickerComponent` (notably the new-goal wizard before the v4.20.6 cascade-dropdown rewrite, but the bug affected any future surface too), the Next button stayed disabled after selecting a player — coach had to click outside the picker before Next became active, or in many cases Next never enabled at all. **Root cause.** `player-search-picker.js:setSelection()` writes the player's id to the hidden input via direct `valueEl.value = String( id )` assignment. The wizard chrome's `wizard-validation.js` listens for `change` / `blur` / `input` events on `[required]` fields to refresh the Next-button `disabled` state. JS-driven `.value =` assignments **don't** fire those events; the validation listener never re-evaluated and Next stayed disabled even though `player_id` was now non-empty. **Fix.** `setSelection()` now dispatches a bubbling `change` event immediately after the value assignment. `wizard-validation.js` (and any future form-level listener) sees the synthetic event, re-runs its `requiredInputs().some( isEmpty )` check, and updates the Next-button state correctly. Legacy fallback path uses `createEvent` + `initEvent` for older browsers without the `Event` constructor; the modern path uses `new Event( 'change', { bubbles: true } )` per WHATWG. **Defence in depth.** Even after #1156 replaced the goal-wizard's autocomplete with cascade dropdowns, this fix matters for every OTHER surface using `PlayerSearchPickerComponent` (player list search, new-evaluation wizard, any future picker consumer). The fix is on the shared component, not the goal-wizard caller. Patch bump. (closes #1157) =

= 4.20.5 — Attendance: REST write-time roster filter + display JOIN on player's team + delete-backfill migration (closes #1148). Pilot diagnostic confirmed that off-roster `is_guest = 0` rows existed for the player attendance report (Hedel JO14-1 showed 30 players, 14 of which were currently on JO13-1, none had any `team_changed` journey events). The JS helper hides off-team rows visually, but the hidden form fields still submit. For admin users that means the entire academy ships in the POST. `ActivitiesRestController::write_attendance` accepted any submitted player_id and wrote `is_guest = 0` with no roster validation. **Piece 1 — REST write-time chokepoint.** `write_attendance` now looks up the activity's `team_id` once, then for each submitted player_id checks the player's current `team_id`. Off-roster ids are silently dropped (with a `session.attendance.dropped_off_roster` warning log carrying activity_id + activity_team_id + the dropped ids + their current team_ids so operators can triage UI / import bugs from logs). Activities with `team_id = 0` (club-wide / legacy) accept any player by design. The explicit guest path (`POST /sessions/{id}/guests` → `is_guest = 1`) remains the only way to record off-roster attendance. **Piece 2 — Display JOIN fix.** `FrontendAttendancePlayerReportView::query()` LEFT JOIN target changes from `t.id = a.team_id` (activity's team) to `t.id = p.team_id` (player's team). Future legitimate mid-season transfers — caught by the audit trail — render with the player's current team in the report, so the operator can scan for roster movement at a glance. **Piece 3 — Migration 0145 (DELETE-not-flip).** Walks every `is_guest = 0` row where `player.team_id != activity.team_id`. For each candidate, checks `tt_player_events` for a `team_changed` event putting the player on the activity's team at or before the activity's `session_date`. If the audit trail justifies the row (player was on the activity's team at the time), the row is preserved as legitimate historical squad attendance. Otherwise the row is DELETED — these are write-path artefacts, not legitimate guest attendance, and reclassifying them as `is_guest = 1` would invent a "guest history" that didn't happen. Two-pass design: pass 1 logs every row to-be-deleted to `tt_logs` with sample ids (full reconstruction available); pass 2 runs the DELETE in 500-row chunks. Idempotent. Conservative — only touches non-guest rows on team-scoped activities. **For the pilot data:** JO14-1 attendance report drops from 30 rows → 16 (the real squad). The 14 JO13-1 artefacts vanish entirely. The JO13-1 report is unaffected — those rows were on JO14-1 activities, never on JO13's. **Out of scope.** The upstream activity edit form's multi-team player pool (#1154) ships as a separate UX-cleanup issue — the REST chokepoint in this PR closes the data integrity gap regardless of whether the form fix lands. The `FrontendAttendanceTeamReportView` doesn't expose the per-row team-display issue (it aggregates per team, not per player). Patch bump. (closes #1148) =

= 4.20.2 — Scouting visits: scout matrix gate fix — tile-declared entity aligned to `prospects` (closes #1143). Pilot reported that scouts hit "Niet geautoriseerd" on `?tt_view=scouting-visits` despite the Permission Chain Debug page (#777) showing `tt_view_prospects` + `tt_edit_prospects` both resolving to `✓ allowed` via `userCanOrMatrix()`. **Root cause:** the denial wasn't from the view's own gate — it was from `DashboardShortcode::matrixDispatchAllows()` one layer up. That helper calls `TileRegistry::entityForViewSlug('scouting-visits')`, which returned `'scouting_visits'` per the tile registration at `CoreSurfaceRegistration.php:625`. But `scouting_visits` is a phantom entity — zero seed rows for any persona in `config/authorization_seed.php`, zero `LegacyCapMapper` entries. So `MatrixGate::canAnyScope($user_id, 'scouting_visits', 'read')` returned false for every non-admin user, and dispatch denied before the view's broader `tt_view_prospects` OR `tt_edit_prospects` gate could pass. The Permission Chain Debug page couldn't surface the cause because it iterates legacy caps; `scouting_visits` is unreachable through that lens. **Fix:** tile's `entity` declaration changes from `scouting_visits` to `prospects`. The tile already declared `cap => tt_view_prospects`; the view's own gate already checks the same caps; scout/HoD/admin all have `prospects.read` globally via the matrix seed. The matrix-dispatch gate now queries `(prospects, read)` and passes through. Single-line change in `CoreSurfaceRegistration.php`. Inline comment documents the rationale next to the changed line so future tile edits don't reflex-reintroduce the phantom-entity pattern. **What's NOT in this PR.** Three previous "scout-prospects auth" fixes (v3.110.147 / .168 / .181) all patched the view's own gate — the wrong layer. They stay in the code untouched; they're still useful when an entity legitimately has both caps wired but a persona-resolution edge case surfaces only one. The architectural lesson — tiles declaring entities that don't exist in the matrix cause silent dispatch denials with no diagnostic page coverage — is worth a follow-up: a boot-time check that walks every tile-declared entity against the matrix-known-entities set and warns when an orphan is registered. Logged as future work, not in scope for this fix. **The `scouting-visit` (singular) slug stays.** It's registered for slug-ownership only (no tile, so `entityForViewSlug()` returns null and the matrix-dispatch gate bypasses on the null check). Detail page already works. Patch bump. (closes #1143) =


= 4.20.1 — Persona-dashboard editor: swap-on-hover for already-placed cards, horizontal gap-fill compact pass, and touch-input fallback via Pointer Events (closes #1142). Pilot 2026-06-03 ask: the editor's drag-drop technically worked but produced fragmented layouts (gaps in rows the operator couldn't recover from), didn't work at all on tablets (HTML5 `draggable` doesn't fire on iOS/Android), and offered no way to swap two cards' positions — every drag pushed colliders down, leaving more gaps. **Swap-on-hover.** Dragging an already-placed canvas card over another card on the grid now lights the target green (`.is-swap-target`) and, on drop, swaps the two slots' (x, y) instead of running the push-down/collision-resolve path. Detected in the existing `dragover` band handler by reading the closest `.tt-pde-card[data-tt-pde-slot]` ancestor of the cursor target; the drop branches in `handleDropOnBand` via a new `swapSlots(srcId, dstId)` helper that resolves any size-mismatch overlap via the existing `resolveCollisions` + `compactGrid` pair. Empty-cell drops keep the push-down/compact behaviour unchanged. **Horizontal gap-fill.** New `packHorizontally(grid)` runs as the final step of `compactGrid` after its vertical pull-up pass. Walks each row top-to-bottom; for each slot, scans every (nx, ny) where the slot would fit without colliding with a preceding slot, and relocates if the candidate is strictly earlier in (y, x) order. Bounded by `grid.length` iterations; converges in 1-3 passes on real layouts. The pilot's fragmented Assistent-trainer dashboard (row 2 KPI card + trailing gap, smaller widget bumped to row 3) now self-tidies after any drop: the row-3 widget gets pulled up into the row-2 gap, no manual recovery needed. **Touch fallback.** New `wireTouchDragFallback()` binds Pointer Events on the canvas root: `pointerdown` (touch / pen only — mouse keeps the native HTML5 DnD) captures the underlying canvas card, sets `__ttPdeDrag = { kind: 'move', slotId }`, spawns a floating ghost via `cloneNode`, and pins it to fixed coordinates that track the finger. `pointermove` runs the same `gridCellFromEvent` + `snapToGuides` + swap-target detection + `previewDragLayout` chain the desktop path uses. `pointerup` synthesises an `{ clientX, clientY, shiftKey }` event-like and feeds it to `handleDropOnBand('grid', synthetic)` so the existing drop logic + swap branch fire unchanged. `pointercancel` / `lostpointercapture` tear down the ghost and clear all visuals. **CSS additions.** `.tt-pde-card.is-swap-target` lights up green with a 3px inset border + 4px halo + light-green fill. `.tt-pde-card[data-tt-pde-band="grid"]` sets `touch-action: none` so the canvas doesn't scroll-jack the pointer-down. `.tt-pde-card.tt-pde-touch-ghost` adds a heavier drop shadow + accent outline + `pointer-events: none` so `document.elementFromPoint` sees the underlying band, not the ghost. **i18n.** New `swapped: "Swapped."` string in the editor bootstrap (Dutch: "Gewisseld."), surfaced by the `setStatus` call after a swap commit. **Keyboard a11y unchanged.** Space-to-grab + arrows + escape still drive `moveSlotByKey` → `resolveCollisions` + `compactGrid` (which now includes the horizontal pack). **Mouse a11y unchanged.** Desktop with a fine pointer keeps the native HTML5 DnD primary; the touch path's `pointerdown` early-returns on `pointerType === 'mouse'`. **Out of scope.** Live-dashboard reorder for the published surface (per-user override layer is a separate feature). Multi-select drag and resize-by-edge-drag remain out of scope. Patch bump within v4.20 series. (closes #1142) =

= 4.20.0 — People — permanent-delete cascade across 9 reference tables + informed-consent impact-preview dialog (closes #1138). Pilot 2026-06-03 ask: every person must be deletable without leaving orphan rows that pollute roster surfaces, scope grants, staff-dev tracking, mentorships, invitations, and player parent-contact links. **Cascade service.** New `Infrastructure\People\PersonDeletionCascade` runs everything in a single transaction. CASCADE-delete classes (the row exists only because the person exists): `tt_team_people`, `tt_user_role_scopes` (rows where `person_id = X`), `tt_staff_development`, `tt_staff_certifications`, `tt_staff_evaluations`, `tt_staff_goals`, `tt_staff_mentorships` (mentor OR mentee = X), `tt_invitations` (pending/expired targets). SET-NULL classes (parent row survives, reference cleared): `tt_user_role_scopes.granted_by_person_id`, `tt_invitations.target_person_id` for accepted invitations, `tt_players.parent_person_id`. No block rules — per the pilot ask, every person is deletable; rows that would orphan get nulled so the parent record renders cleanly as "no person assigned". Any per-table failure rolls the entire batch back. **WP user stays.** The `wp_users` table is NOT touched; the audit-log + impersonation-log + evaluations + goals + activities that reference `wp_users.ID` via `created_by` / `coach_id` etc. are unaffected. The operator deletes the WP account separately via WP's Users admin if desired (same separation precedent as migration 0139). **Audit-log entry** `person.deleted_with_cascade` carries `person_ids`, `club_id`, `deleted` count, per-table counts, nulled counts, and `by_user` so post-hoc verification has full context. **REST preview endpoint** `POST /wp-json/talenttrack/v1/people/delete-preview` accepts `{ ids: [N, N, N] }` and returns a per-person impact summary — read-only, no writes, cap-gated on `tt_edit_settings`. Response shape includes human-readable team names + role labels + player names so the dialog renders strings, not raw ids. Capped at 100 ids per call. **wp-admin dialog.** `assets/js/admin-people-delete-preview.js` + `assets/css/admin-people-delete-preview.css` intercept the bulk-action form submit when the chosen action is `delete_permanent` on the People list, fetch the preview, and open a structured `<dialog>` showing per-person CASCADE + SET-NULL impact. Two-step type-DELETE confirm triggers for batches ≥ 3 persons OR any person with ≥ 5 affected references; trivial deletes (1 person with ≤ 2 refs) skip the type-DELETE step so the everyday case isn't tedious. Mobile-first per CLAUDE.md §2 — width clamps to 96vw at ≤ 480px, footer buttons stack full-width, body scrolls when impact list is long. **WP user-account note** rendered inside the dialog body so the operator understands what is and isn't being deleted. **No schema migration** — the cascade reads existing columns; all involved tables already exist (since 0006, 0025, 0048, 0050, 0062). **Patch route stays.** The frontend `DELETE /people/{id}` REST stays as a soft-archive (no destructive cascade triggered from REST) — only the wp-admin "Delete permanently" bulk action runs `PersonDeletionCascade`. **Cap gating.** Hard-delete still requires `tt_edit_settings` at the bulk-action handler; the preview endpoint and dialog enqueue carry the same cap. **Out of scope.** Cascade for other entity types (Players, Teams, Activities, Evaluations, Goals) each have their own reference graphs and ship separately when the People pattern is validated. WP user deletion remains a manual step in WP Users admin. Minor bump — first feature in the v4.20 series. (closes #1138) =

= 4.19.12 — People REST: `archive_person()` no longer silently fails when no row matches (closes #1137). Pilot reported that clicking Archive on a person detail returned to the list with the success toast — but the person remained on the list, unchanged. **Root cause:** `PeopleRestController::archive_person()` issued `$wpdb->update()` and only treated `$ok === false` as failure. `$wpdb->update()` returns `0` (not `false`) when the WHERE clause matches no rows — for example when the person's `club_id` doesn't match the current operator's club, or when the row is already archived by another tab. The handler treated that zero as success, returned 200, and the `frontend-archive-button.js` redirected to the list as designed. The row was never touched. **Fix:** a new `$ok === 0` branch in `archive_person()` returns 404 `not_found` with a Dutch-translated "Person not found in your club." message, and logs `rest.person.archive.no_row` with the `id` + `club_id` context so the same surface can be triaged from logs without the operator describing the steps. The existing `$ok === false` branch keeps returning 500 `db_error` for genuine SQL failures (e.g. lock timeout, constraint violation) so the two error classes don't collapse into one bucket. **Frontend behaviour.** The archive button JS already routes any non-2xx response into its error path — the user now sees a clear "Person not found in your club" notice instead of a silent redirect, and the page stays on the detail view so they can take a screenshot or report the cross-club mismatch. No JS change needed. **Out of scope.** A site-admin override that could archive a person regardless of club scope (today: archive is club-scoped by design); a Restore affordance for archived people (issue body Suspect D — separate UX, not a regression). Patch bump. (closes #1137) =

= 4.18.0 — Evaluations: touch-friendly rating input — chip grid + inline-slider rows (closes #1067). Replaces the typed-number rating input wherever a coach captures a rating. Spec / design-of-record lives at `.local-mockups/player-rating-input/` (designed in pilot session 2026-06-01). The typed-number pattern was hostile on the sideline: tap field → numeric keyboard pops → tap "7" → tap "." → tap "5" → dismiss keyboard, repeated 10–30× per player on a multi-category eval. **New component `\TT\Shared\Frontend\Components\RatingInputComponent`.** Two render methods, one component: `renderSingle( $args )` emits a chip grid — 11 chips at the default 5.0–10.0/0.5 scale arranged 4-per-row with a filler cell, half-step values visually lighter than whole numbers, one tap commits a final value, no keyboard. `renderListRow( $args )` emits a slider row — label + range slider + tabular value readout in a 78px/flex/34px grid that fits at 360px with all four canonical category names (Technical / Tactical / Physical / Mental). Both methods read `rating_min` / `rating_max` / `rating_step` from `tt_config` (default 5/10/0.5) so a club running a different scale just changes config. Schema is `DECIMAL(4,1)` — half-step values flow through unchanged. `label_hidden` option on `renderListRow` lets host markup own the label column when the slider drops into an existing table layout (e.g. HybridDeepRateStep's `<th>`/`<td>` rows). **CSS `assets/css/components/rating-input.css`.** Mobile-first. Chips ≥ 48×48 with 8px gap; slider hit area 36px tall, thumb 28×28 with 3px white halo for visibility against the accent track. `:focus-visible` outlines for keyboard, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured. Sub-rows indented 20px. **JS `assets/js/components/rating-input.js`.** Vanilla; no dependencies. Wires chip clicks to a hidden input + dispatches a synthetic `change` so host forms react. Slider input event updates the readout span. The "empty" state — slider sits at the midpoint visually for thumb visibility but the row carries `data-tt-rating-empty="1"` so server-side and JS treat it as unrated — clears on first interaction. On form submit, any slider still flagged empty has its `name` attribute stripped so the value doesn't post; the server then receives only real coach picks. Arrow-key navigation between chips matches native radiogroup behaviour. **Dropped into four surfaces.** `PostGameEvaluationForm` and `PlayerSelfEvaluationForm` (single overall rating → chip grid). `RateActorsStep` (per-category multi-player rate grid — main category row + nested sub-category rows → inline-slider rows). `HybridDeepRateStep` (player self-eval per-category → inline-slider rows with `label_hidden=true` to fit the existing `<th>` label column). **Server-side validate() upgraded to floats.** `RateActorsStep::validate` and `HybridDeepRateStep::validate` now cast incoming rating values to float + snap-to-0.5 instead of `(int)`-truncating to whole numbers (which would have silently flattened a 7.5 pick to 7). The wizard state read also casts to float so the input pre-fill survives a step-back round trip. `EvaluationInserter` mirrors the float+snap before writing to `tt_eval_ratings`. **Existing roster JS preserved.** The per-player status pill + overall progress counter in `RateActorsStep` checks the sliders the same way it checked the number inputs (`.tt-rate-input` selector); the only new behaviour is skipping sliders with `data-tt-rating-empty` from the "filled" count. The sub-cat → main-cat auto-compute (rounded average of non-zero subs written back to the main category) still works — now reads/writes floats, snaps to 0.5, and mirrors the value into the main row's readout span so the visual stays in sync. **Asset enqueue** at three hosts: the two wizard steps register the handles in their `render()`, and `FrontendTaskDetailView` (the workflow task surface) enqueues unconditionally on every task detail (low cost, simple). Idempotent — same handles across surfaces. **Out of scope.** Re-skinning the flat `CoachForms::renderEvalForm` legacy eval surface (the canonical surface per CLAUDE.md §3 is the wizard, which this PR covers). The wizard-chrome step-indicator is unrelated. Minor bump — new user-visible component, four surfaces upgraded. Strings via `__()`; .po sync lands next CI cycle. (closes #1067) =

= 4.17.6 — Persona dashboard editor: visibility-hint badge per slot (closes #1102). Pilot triage 2026-06-01 surfaced after #1104 unblocked AC's dashboard: ~12 widgets/tiles were configured for the Assistent-trainer persona but only 3 rendered, because the typical AC user (`tt_coach` WP role) lacked the caps the underlying widgets / tiles gate on. The editor had no feedback — admins drop widgets onto a persona's template, the layout publishes, and the widget silently vanishes for the persona's typical user at render time. This ship adds a small green-check / amber-warning line in the slot properties detail block so the admin sees the visibility outcome at *configure* time, not pilot-test time. **PHP — bootstrap payload.** `EditorPage::buildBootstrap()` now publishes three new fields the editor JS consumes: (1) `default_role_for_persona` — `{ persona_slug: wp_role_slug }` map. New `PersonaResolver::defaultWpRoleFor( persona )` inverts the `WP_ROLE_TO_PERSONA` constant and hard-codes `head_coach` / `assistant_coach` → `tt_coach` since those split at runtime. (2) `role_caps` — `{ wp_role_slug: { cap_name: true, ... } }` map. One entry per WP role any of the in-scope personas might map to, sourced from WP's `get_role()->capabilities`. (3) `tile_caps_by_slug` — `{ view_slug: cap }` map sourced from `TileRegistry::allRegistered()` so the JS can compute the effective cap for a `navigation_tile` widget (whose own `cap_required` is empty — the cap lives on the underlying tile slug it points at). **JS — `renderDetailBlock` now persona-aware.** Takes `activePersona` (= `state.persona`, the persona currently being edited). For widgets with a `cap_required`, and for `navigation_tile` slots whose chosen data source maps to a `tile_caps_by_slug` entry, the editor resolves the effective cap, compares it against the active persona's default-role caps, and renders a one-line badge under the "Capability required" line: green ✓ "Visible to %s users by default" when the role holds the cap; amber ⚠ "Hidden — %s users lack `cap` by default. Grant via Authorization → Matrix or remove from this layout." when it doesn't. Both lines include an italic caveat line clarifying the check is against the persona's *default* WP role only — per-user matrix scopes can override either way. **JS — re-renders live.** Changing the data source on a `navigation_tile` slot calls `commit()` → `renderAll()` → `renderProperties()` → `renderDetailBlock()`, so the hint updates as the admin tries different slugs. **CSS.** Two new classes — `.tt-pde-detail-vis--ok` (subtle green tint) and `.tt-pde-detail-vis--blocked` (subtle amber tint) — sit just under the existing `.tt-pde-detail-cap` line. Caveat span is greyer + italic so the badge reads as advisory, not blocking. **What this is NOT.** Not a hard block — admins can still publish layouts with amber-flagged widgets (a per-user matrix scope might grant the cap to *some* users with that persona even if the role default doesn't, e.g. an Assistent-trainer who's also been given a per-user `tt_view_evaluations` cap). Not a runtime change — the GridRenderer / TileRegistry visibility filters are unchanged. This is purely an editor-time hint. **Caveats / known limitations** (parked for follow-up if pilot reports). (a) The check uses the *default* WP role's caps, not the persona's matrix entitlements. Cap-bridged matrix entries (e.g. `evaluations:read` for `head_coach`) won't show in `role_caps` unless the bridge already wrote them to the WP role at boot. For tooling-time hints this is acceptable; a precise check would query the matrix per-persona instead, which is bigger work. (b) Hint depends on `state.persona`, not a hypothetical preview user, so the editor answers "if a user with the persona's default WP role looked at this, would they see it?" — matches the question the admin is asking. **Verification.** Open Admin → Dashboard-lay-outs → Assistent-trainer. Click the Podium tile slot (or any slot configured for AC that AC's matrix doesn't grant). The detail block now shows an amber ⚠ line naming the missing cap. Switch the dropdown to Hoofdtrainer — the same slot shows a green ✓. Patch bump. (closes #1102) =

= 4.17.4 — Authorization: deterministic person lookup + dedupe migration for duplicate `tt_people` rows (closes #1104). Pilot triage 2026-06-01 surfaced the real cause of the empty Assistent-trainer dashboard symptom we'd been chasing: the AC test user (wp_user_id=10) had **two active tt_people rows** (id=7 and id=30) for the same WP user in the same club. `AuthorizationService::getPersonIdByUserId` did `SELECT id FROM tt_people WHERE wp_user_id=%d AND status='active' AND club_id=%d LIMIT 1` with no `ORDER BY`. MySQL returned id=7 (lowest PK in practice, but non-deterministic). The team-people bridge then looked for assignments on `person_id=7` — none. Zero resolved scopes, zero dashboard tiles, even though the admin Persoon edit page (which reads the real row, id=30) showed the team assignment. Two sources of truth silently disagreed for the entire pilot session. **Resolver hardening (`AuthorizationService::getPersonIdByUserId`).** Added `ORDER BY id DESC` to the `LIMIT 1`. Picks the most-recently-created active row when duplicates exist — same tiebreak the dedupe migration uses so resolver + cleanup agree. Existing callers behave identically when no duplicates exist (the typical case). **New helper `AuthorizationService::findAllActivePersonIdsByUserId`.** Returns every active person_id linked to a WP user in the current club. Used by the Rechten-diagnose page to surface the duplicate-detection warning. **Application guards in `PeopleRepository::create()` + `update()`.** Block a second active person record from claiming a WP user that another active row already owns in this club. Inactive rows are allowed to share `wp_user_id` (they don't resolve). Returns `false` on collision — matches the existing repository error pattern. **Dedupe migration `0139_dedupe_tt_people_by_wp_user.php`.** Finds every `(wp_user_id, club_id)` cluster with > 1 active row. Per cluster, picks the winner: most `tt_team_people` rows referencing the person id first, then highest `id` (newest). Sets losers to `status='inactive'` — NOT deleted, so operators can revive any inactivated row from the People admin. Logs the winner/loser mapping to `tt_audit_log` under `action='person.deduped'` with payload `{ wp_user_id, winner_id, winner_rel_cnt, loser_id, loser_rel_cnt }` for forensic recovery. Forward-only; idempotent. **Rechten-diagnose warning hint.** When a WP user has > 1 active person_id, the diagnose page now renders a red ⚠ row listing all linked Persoon ids with edit links and a one-line explanation pointing at #1104 + migration 0139. The two-source disagreement is what made the original triage three hours; the warning makes the next occurrence ten minutes. **Verification.** On Casper's install the manual DELETE of the duplicate row (Persoon #7) made AC's dashboard render the full configured layout immediately — confirming the duplicate was the symptom's root cause. The shipped migration automates the same fix on every install at upgrade time. Patch bump — bug fix, no operator-breaking change. (closes #1104) =

= 4.15.7 — Blueprint editor: picking a player no longer silently fails (closes #1054). Pilot bug surfaced 2026-05-31: coach picks a player from the slot picker, page reloads, slot stays empty, no error shown. The end-to-end trace was: JS PUT to `/blueprints/{id}/assignment` carried a perfectly valid `{ slot_label, tier, ref: { kind: 'player', player_id: 52 } }` body — but the slot stayed empty on every browser. Root cause was three-layered: (1) `TeamBlueprintsRepository::setAssignment` called `wpdb->insert/update/delete` and never checked the return value — when the INSERT collided on a UNIQUE constraint the failure was swallowed and `true` was returned anyway, (2) `set_blueprint_assignment` REST handler then returned `200 OK` to the client, (3) the JS reloaded the page believing the assignment had landed. **The underlying INSERT collision** was rooted in migration 0129's UNIQUE constraint `uniq_slot_tier (blueprint_id, slot_label, tier)` — no `club_id` — combined with `setAssignment`'s SELECT-before-INSERT that DID filter by `club_id`. Any stale row for the same `(blueprint_id, slot_label, tier)` but a different `club_id` made the SELECT miss it and the INSERT collide. **The fix.** Migration 0135 widens the UNIQUE to `uniq_slot_tier_club (club_id, blueprint_id, slot_label, tier)` so the constraint matches how the repo logically scopes assignments (and stays correct under future SaaS multi-tenancy where `CurrentClub::id()` returns ≠1). `setAssignment` now checks every `wpdb` return value, captures `wpdb->last_error`, and returns `false` on DB-layer failure; new `lastError()` accessor exposes the message. The REST controller calls `setAssignment`, returns `500` with the captured error when persistence failed, and turns malformed-player-ref payloads (caller sent `kind=player` but no usable `player_id`) into a `400` via a new `\InvalidArgumentException` path in `coerceAssignmentRef` — previously these were silently coerced to `null` and triggered a slot DELETE. The JS `refForRosterEntry` guard returns `null` rather than building `{ kind: 'player', player_id: NaN }`; `saveAssignment` short-circuits with a localised alert when the ref is malformed, reads the server's error message out of the response body on `!ok`, and verifies the response payload contains the persisted ref before reloading (so a regression that returned 200 OK + ref:null would no longer silently "succeed"). New i18n string `bad_ref`. **Pilot impact**: blueprint editor's primary interaction works again on every install where stale rows might exist; on installs where the silent-fail wasn't surfacing, every layer is now defensive enough that a future regression would surface as a visible alert instead of a vanishing pick. Patch bump. (closes #1054) =

= 4.15.6 — Methodology seed top-up: Omschakelen leerdoelen + Spelinzicht/Communicatie sub-actions (closes #1061). = 4.15.5 — REST: `BaseController::isPositiveInt()` must be public, not protected (closes #1057). Saving any lookup value returned HTTP 500 with `Uncaught TypeError: call_user_func(): Argument #1 ($callback) must be a valid callback, cannot access protected method TT\Infrastructure\REST\LookupsRestController::isPositiveInt()`. Four controllers (LookupsRestController, InvitationsRestController, LookupNormalisationRestController, PushSubscriptionsRestController) register routes with `'validate_callback' => [ self::class, 'isPositiveInt' ]` against URL segments that need positive-integer validation. The validator lives on `BaseController` as `protected static`, which works fine for internal calls but breaks when WP REST invokes the callback via PHP's `call_user_func()` — that runs outside the class hierarchy and cannot reach protected methods even on a subclass. The route-arg validation step 500s before the handler ever runs. One-line fix: promote `BaseController::isPositiveInt()` to `public`. Every PUT / DELETE on `/lookups/{type}/{id}`, every invitation endpoint that takes an id, and the push-subscriptions endpoint all start working again. Pilot impact: any operator who tried to edit a lookup value on a live install since v4.11.0 (when this validator pattern was introduced) would have hit the 500 — surfaced today during the post-drain pilot pass on the Posities lookup admin. Patch bump. (closes #1057) =

= 4.15.1 — Match execution: attendance + minutes recompute on PENDING_REVIEW edits and on Finalize (closes #1048, #1033 follow-up C). v4.15.0 introduced PENDING_REVIEW with editable score / sub / goal endpoints, but `tt_attendance` (status + minutes_played per player) was only written once during `route_finish`. Any subsequent edit in PENDING_REVIEW left the derived attendance totals stale until... nothing, because the one-shot write never re-fired. **Recompute extracted to the repository.** New `MatchExecutionRepository::recomputeAttendanceAndMinutes( $execution_id )` owns the attendance + minutes write loop that used to live inline in `route_finish`. Reloads the prep snapshot, runs `computeMinutes()` against the current substitution log, reconciles stale rows (the #1032 sweep), and writes status + `minutes_played` for every player in the prep's availability list. Idempotent — same prep + same sub log → same attendance rows. **Trigger pattern.** Per the user's "both" decision (2026-05-30): the recompute fires (a) on every PENDING_REVIEW edit (substitution log changes, goal-event add / delete) via a new `recomputeIfPendingReview()` helper that gates by the current state, AND (b) on Finalize as a belt-and-braces pass before the FINALIZED flip closes the window for missed writes (offline-queue replay, transient DB errors). Live writes during the match still skip the recompute — they happen too often, and `route_finish` covers the transition. Score edits also skip (a score change doesn't touch any input to `computeMinutes`). **Failure handling.** Per the locked default: on recompute exception the method swallows the error, logs at warn level via `Logger::warn( 'match_execution.recompute_failed', … )` with the execution_id, and returns false. The caller's primary action (the edit, the finalize) has already succeeded — aborting an edit because a side effect failed would be hostile, and the next edit or finalize will re-fire the recompute. **route_finish refactor.** The inline attendance + minutes write block (76 lines) is replaced with a single `$repo->recomputeAttendanceAndMinutes( $exec_id )` call. Behaviour-identical for the End-match tap path. **Out of scope.** Async / background recompute — inline is fine, ~20 attendance rows max per execution. Recompute on live-trio writes — preserved as today's behaviour. No schema, no REST surface change, no new caps. Patch bump. (closes #1048) =

= 4.15.0 — Match execution: pending-review state + Finalize action (partial #1033, MVP). Pilot ask: "after the match when I complete the match the match execution should move to a separate place where they all are stored and where they can be viewed and adjusted when needed." Today, tapping "End match" makes the execution immediately read-only — no opportunity to fix a missed goal, a wrongly-timed sub, or a missed score-tap. **State machine extended.** `MatchExecutionState` enum gains two values: `PENDING_REVIEW` (post-match, editable) and `FINALIZED` (terminal, read-only). The legacy `FINISHED` constant is kept as a deprecated alias for one release; migration `0133_match_execution_state_pending_review` backfills any existing `state='finished'` row to `'finalized'` (safe interpretation — those rows were closed at a time without the new edit affordance). New `EDITABLE` set (live trio + PENDING_REVIEW) drives the write-guard. **REST.** Tapping "End match" (`route_finish`) now lands the execution in `PENDING_REVIEW` instead of `FINISHED`, but still writes attendance + minutes + flips the activity to completed — every existing post-match consumer keeps working. New `route_finalize` (`POST /match-execution/{activity_id}/finalize`) transitions PENDING_REVIEW → FINALIZED. Score / substitution / goal-event / goal-event-delete endpoints gain a single-line `assertEditable()` guard that returns HTTP 409 when the execution is FINALIZED. NOT_STARTED still accepts writes (offline-queue replay tolerance). **View.** A new post-match status section renders above the existing footer when state ∈ {PENDING_REVIEW, FINALIZED}: an amber pill ("Match ended · pending review") or grey pill ("Finalized — read-only"). PENDING_REVIEW additionally shows a red "Finalize match" button + a one-line warning "Locks the match. Goals, subs, and score cannot be edited after." A tiny inline IIFE wires the button to the new `/finalize` endpoint with a confirm prompt and a reload on success. **Out of scope for this MVP (filed as #1033 follow-ups for the next analyst pass).** Dedicated listing surface (`?tt_view=match-executions`) so coaches can find every pending-review or finalized match without going through activity detail; "Matches needing review" widget on the coach hero; auto-recompute of attendance + minutes when subs are edited in PENDING_REVIEW (today's behaviour: attendance/minutes write once at `route_finish` and don't recompute on later edits); explicit "late-event" affordance with a retroactive minute picker; mockup additions for the pending-review + finalized states. v1 ships the spine of the feature (state machine + Finalize + edit-guards) — the surfaces around it follow in scoped follow-ups. **Why a minor bump.** New state, new endpoint, new visible UI affordance. Migration 0133 is additive only (no schema change — just data backfill). No new caps. (partial #1033) =

= 4.14.1 — Standard report: minutes played per team / player (closes #1034). New curated analytics report at `?tt_view=minutes-report-team&team_id=N&from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&type=all|League|Cup|Friendly`. Pre-built answer to "how is game-time distributed across the squad?" — the question the pilot academy asked for explicitly and that today can only be answered via CSV export. **Layout.** Per the locked mockup at `.local-mockups/standard-reports/minutes-played/index.html` (Option A — squad table). = 4.13.3 — Rate-players step pulls from the actual on-pitch set (closes #1032). After a match-execution finished, the rate-players wizard step surfaced too many people in the roster — bench / unused subs (`minutes_played = 0`), players from other teams via stale attendance rows, and the existing v4.3.20 linked-guest support gave no visual cue why "another team's player" appeared. Root cause: `RateActorsStep::ratablePlayersForActivity()` read `tt_attendance` — club-scoped only, with no team filter, no minutes filter, and downstream of the match-finish endpoint that INSERTs an attendance row for every available player including bench (`MatchExecutionRestController.php:246-272`). Stale rows from prior runs were never reconciled. **The rate-step now pulls from the actual on-pitch set for match-type activities.** New `ratablePlayersForMatch( $activity_id, $team_id )` collects the `DISTINCT player_id` set from `tt_match_prep_lineup` (starting XI per half) UNION `tt_match_execution_substitutions.player_on_id` (excluding `reversed_at` events), then SELECTs the resolved player rows with an `is_guest` flag derived by comparing `pl.team_id` against the activity's team. Bench-only players are excluded by construction. Already-rated guard preserved. For training and any non-match activity (`activity_type_key NOT IN ('match','game')`), the legacy attendance-based query stays — there is no lineup data to derive from. **Guest pill on rate-step rows.** Rows where `pl.team_id` differs from the activity's `team_id` carry a `Guest` pill between the player name and the status pill, with a tooltip "On loan from another team for this match." Answers the "why is this other-team player here?" surprise the user surfaced. **Stale-attendance reconciliation in finish endpoint.** Before the per-availability INSERT/UPDATE loop, the finish endpoint now DELETEs any `tt_attendance` row for the activity whose `player_id` is NOT in the prep's availability list — when match-execution finishes, availability is the source of truth. Eliminates the cross-list contamination from prior mark-attendance runs. **Out of scope.** Wizard-loop symptom (bug 3 in the issue) is downstream of the wizard-restart fix #1006 and gets re-tested after that lands; the rate-step → behaviour-step transition itself is unchanged. The lineup / subs schema doesn't carry an `is_guest` column, so guest detection is derived from `tt_players.team_id` instead of a per-event flag — works for the pilot's model where guests are players from sibling teams already in the club. No schema, no REST, no new caps. Patch bump. (closes #1032) =

= 4.13.2 — Match prep print: dedicated route so admin bar + theme chrome stay off paper (closes #1031). = 4.13.1 — Lookup admin: internal-key now populates on row click, locales render one-per-row (closes #1037, #1038). Two related bugs on the list-first lookup admin (`?tt_view=lookups&type=<…>`), bundled because they share the same file and the same root design pattern. **#1037 — Internal-key field empty on row click.** `FrontendConfigurationView::renderLookupFormViews()` rendered TWO `<form data-tt-lkp-form>` elements when the page loaded without `?edit=N` — one inside `tt-lkp-view-add`, one inside `tt-lkp-view-edit`. `lookup-admin.js` used `querySelector('[data-tt-lkp-form]')` which returns the first match, so it bound to the form inside `view-add` (hidden by default). Clicking a row populated the hidden form; the visible form (in `view-edit`) stayed blank — internal key, sort order, translations all empty. Fix: collapse to ONE form inside a single `tt-lkp-view-form` section. CSS now maps both `data-state="add"` and `data-state="edit"` to `view-form`. The form's heading + hint flip between "Add new value" / "Edit value" via new `data-tt-lkp-form-title` and `data-tt-lkp-name-hint` hooks driven by `clearForm()` / `populateFromRow()`; four new i18n keys (`title_add`, `title_edit`, `hint_add`, `hint_edit`) carry the strings through to JS. **#1038 — Translation locales render in messy grid.** When `show_desc=false` (positions, evaluation categories, etc.), the desktop ≥640px breakpoint set the translations grid to 3 columns and hid the empty `<span class="tt-lkp-tx-cell-desc">` spacer with `display:none`. `display:none` removes the element from grid auto-flow, so the next locale badge fell into the empty third column instead of starting a new row — five locales of two visible cells each wrapped into a 3-column grid produced badges and inputs in the wrong places. Fix: drop the desktop 3-column variant entirely and the empty-spacer span at the source. The grid is now always 2 columns (locale | input); description spans columns 2/-1 on its own row when present. Mobile-first compliant, one-locale-per-row at every viewport. **Out of scope**: side-panel master-detail layout (#1039) — builds on this clean single-form base. No schema, no REST, no caps change. Patch bump. (closes #1037, closes #1038) =

= 4.12.10 — PHPStan rule — vocabulary constants enforcement (PR-set 8 of 8, closes #988 umbrella). Final PR-set in the #988 umbrella migration. Lands the custom PHPStan rule that flags raw string-literal comparisons against any value already enumerated under `TT\Domain\Vocabularies\Lookups\*` or `TT\Domain\Vocabularies\Enums\*` — the regression gate that prevents PR-sets 1-7's work from silently un-doing itself as new code lands. Rule class `TT\Tests\PhpStanRules\VocabularyConstantsRule` walks `BinaryOp\Identical` / `NotIdentical` / `Equal` / `NotEqual` AST nodes plus `in_array($value, [...], $strict)` calls; for each string literal it cross-references against the `const ALL` arrays in the 29 vocabulary classes (built lazily via reflection so new vocabularies land in subsequent PR-sets without rule edits) and emits an error suggesting the typed constant (`AttendanceStatus::PRESENT` instead of `'present'`). Out of scope by design: switch / match arms, SQL string literals, array keys, default-parameter literals, migration-seed values — those are either canonical-stored-value contexts (DB layer is the source of truth) or refactors better handled as a separate sweep. Per #988's locked decisions (2026-05-28), the rule ships as **infrastructure but disabled by default** — the backwards-compat allowlist (REST endpoints accept BOTH the raw literal AND the typed constant for one release) keeps the raw literals legal until the deprecation window closes; flipping the rule into the default analyse run today would flood the build with errors on the same call sites the allowlist deliberately tolerates. Wire-up is via the opt-in overlay `tests/PhpStanRules/vocabulary-constants-rule.neon` — operators include that file from their own `phpstan.local.neon` to run the rule on demand (and CI will flip to it once the allowlist sunsets in the next minor). `composer.json` gains an `autoload-dev` PSR-4 mapping for `TT\Tests\PhpStanRules\` -> `tests/PhpStanRules/` so the rule class is autoloadable to PHPStan without bleeding into the runtime plugin classmap. The two existing files under `src/Domain/Vocabularies/` (`Lookups/` 27 classes + `Enums/` 2 classes) are unchanged — PR-set 8 is pure tooling, no behaviour change, no schema, no REST, no UI. **Approximate impact at error-level today** (rough grep against `src/`, excluding `Vocabularies/` itself): low hundreds of comparison sites would be flagged; PR-sets 1-7 already swapped the highest-traffic ones to constants, so the residual is the long tail of one-off comparisons across the codebase plus the REST-allowlist call sites the deprecation contract explicitly tolerates. Closes the #988 umbrella issue. Patch bump — tooling only. (closes #988 umbrella, PR-set 8 of 8) =

= 4.12.1 — PlayerAttendanceCalculator queried `tt_attendance.status` with TitleCase literals `'Present'` / `'Absent'` / `'Excused'`, but the canonical contract codified in `TT\Domain\Vocabularies\Lookups\AttendanceStatus` (v4.11.1, #988 PR-set 1) stores the column in lowercase (`'present'` / `'absent'` / `'excused'`) — the calculator's three SQL CASE expressions silently never matched, so attendance score / streak / status verdicts in `src/Infrastructure/PlayerStatus/` were computing against an empty bucketing of the rows the calculator HAD pulled in. The numerator collapsed to 0 on every call; `low_confidence` fired on every player. Pilot symptom: every player's dashboard attendance card showed either 0% or `null` even on players with full attendance history. Fix replaces the three TitleCase literals with `$wpdb->prepare(... %s ...)` placeholders bound to `AttendanceStatus::PRESENT|ABSENT|EXCUSED`; `use TT\Domain\Vocabularies\Lookups\AttendanceStatus;` added at the top of `PlayerAttendanceCalculator.php`. No data migration needed — `tt_attendance.status` is created with `DEFAULT 'present'` lowercase at install time (Activator.php), and the legacy back-fill from the boolean `present` column also writes lowercase, so no legacy rows carry TitleCase values that would need normalising. The other TitleCase call sites surfaced by the same grep (EvidencePacket.php, ActivitiesRestController.php, LabelTranslator.php, MatchExecutionRestController.php, FrontendMatchExecutionView.php, LookupCanonicalSeeds.php, DemoData\Generators\ActivityGenerator.php, Excel\ExcelImporter.php, migration 0093's seed colours) are part of the #988 umbrella's planned PR-sets and stay out of scope for this targeted bug fix. Patch bump — silent-data-miss bug fix. (closes #996) =

= 4.12.0 — Lookup canonical-language drift audit + admin review tool (closes #987). The `tt_lookups.name` column is contractually the stable English internal key; `tt_translations` carries the per-locale display label. Pilot installs ended up with a mixed-language vocabulary in the column because earlier operator workflows let admins type anything into `name` and never populated `tt_translations` — opening any lookup category showed a list that was half Dutch, half English. This release ships the data fix without changing the schema. New `LookupCanonicalSeeds` class is the single source of truth for canonical English values per `lookup_type`, with a reverse map (drifted-NL -> canonical-EN) seeded from migration 0060's English+Dutch pairs and case-insensitive matching for lowercase drifts like `present` -> `Present`. New migration 0132 walks every `tt_lookups` row, cross-checks `name` against the canonical seed map, and writes a `lookup.needs_review` entry to `tt_audit_log` for every drifted row — current value, suggested canonical, detected source locale, full canonical option list. Idempotent: re-running the migration on an already-audited install skips rows whose entity_id already has an open review entry. The migration never auto-renames anything — every accepted rewrite goes through the human-in-the-loop admin tool. New frontend view `?tt_view=lookup-normalisation` (cap `tt_access_frontend_admin`, mirrors `FrontendConfigurationView`'s gate) lists the pending-review queue: one card per row, with the current value, a dropdown of canonical options pre-selected to the migration's suggestion, and a locale dropdown defaulting to the detected source. Per-row Accept rewrites `tt_lookups.name` to the chosen canonical AND upserts the drifted value as a `tt_translations` entry in the selected locale, so dashboards keep showing the operator-visible Dutch/English label via the existing `LookupTranslator` resolution chain. Per-row Skip leaves the row as-is and records the operator's deliberate decision. Both actions write follow-up `lookup.normalisation.applied` / `lookup.normalisation.skipped` audit entries; the queue join filters resolved rows out so the row stops surfacing without mutating the original audit entry (audit log is append-only by design). New REST endpoints `POST /lookup-normalisation/{audit_id}/accept|skip` under the existing `talenttrack/v1` namespace, both gated on `tt_access_frontend_admin`. Accept defensively rejects canonical values that aren't in the per-`lookup_type` allowlist, so an operator can't typo a fresh drift back into the column. New Configuration tile "Lookup canonical-language review" appears only while there are pending rows (with a count in the description) — it disappears the moment the queue empties. Mobile-first per CLAUDE.md §2: 360px base, 640px breakpoint, all interactive targets >= 48px tall, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected via the existing site CSS. No schema change beyond audit-log writes; no breaking REST change; no behaviour change for end users (the translator chain keeps surfacing the correct locale label whether `name` is `Aanwezig` or `Present`). Minor bump — new admin surface + new audit-log workflow. (closes #987) =

= 4.5.1 — Match prep roster query + wizard activity_id round-trip (#940 / #965 follow-up). Two related defects on the match-prep flow, one architectural class. **(1)** `AvailabilityStep::rosterForActivity()` and `FrontendMatchPrepView::loadTeamRosterById()` both queried a `tt_team_players` junction table that doesn't exist in the schema — `tt_players.team_id` is the canonical FK (verified across 8+ call sites in `Infrastructure/Stats`, `Infrastructure/Security`, `Infrastructure/REST`, etc.). The query returned an empty roster regardless of how many players the team has, so the wizard fell into the "No players on this team yet" early-return branch (pilot symptom on a U14 with a full roster). Same defect class in the main `?tt_view=match-prep` form's roster lookup. Fix: replace the junction join with a direct `SELECT FROM tt_players WHERE team_id = ? AND club_id = ? AND archived_at IS NULL ORDER BY last_name, first_name`. **(2)** Because the wizard's empty-roster branch `return`s before emitting the hidden `<input name="activity_id">`, every subsequent form POST landed at `AvailabilityStep::validate()` with `$post['activity_id']` missing. The wizard also lacked an `initialState()` seed hook, so the URL's `?activity_id=N` was never persisted to wizard state. Result: clicking Create on a wizard with the empty-roster fallback yielded a "Missing activity_id" error — exactly the pilot symptom. Fix: `MatchPrepWizard` now implements `WizardInterface::initialState()` mirroring the mark-attendance pattern; `FrontendWizardView::render()` calls it on first hit and stows `activity_id` in state. After this fix the wizard is resilient even if a future regression takes the empty-roster branch again — the activity_id survives the round-trip. **Why this regressed now**: the #940 admin-post.php switch made the round-trip dependent on `state`, not `$_GET`, because the wizard's POST is processed at admin-post.php (which doesn't carry the original entry URL's query string). Pre-#940 the form POSTed to the dashboard URL itself, so `$_GET['activity_id']` survived. The roster-table bug is older and was masked by the working `$_GET` fallback. Patch bump — bug fix completing the #940 admin-post switch's coverage of the match-prep wizard. (closes follow-up to #940) =

= 4.3.22 — Wizard `submit()` post-create redirect — strip admin-post.php from the redirect base (#940 follow-up). Pilot symptom: clicking Create on the new-team-blueprint wizard sent the coach to `/wp-admin/admin-post.php?tt_view=team-blueprints&id=2` instead of the dashboard URL. Root cause was a direct consequence of the v4.3.16 admin-post.php switch: wizard step `submit()` handlers (notably `Modules/Wizards/TeamBlueprint/ReviewStep::submit()`) build their post-create redirect via `WizardEntryPoint::currentDashboardUrl()`, which reads `$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']`. During admin-post.php processing the request URI is `/wp-admin/admin-post.php`, not the dashboard page, so the helper returned a bogus base. Fix: `WizardEntryPoint::currentDashboardUrl()` consults a per-process override stashed by the admin-post wizard handler. `FrontendWizardView::handleAdminPostStep()` installs the override (the return URL stripped of wizard-specific query args via the new `dashboardOnly()` helper) before invoking any step methods, so every `submit()` that calls `currentDashboardUrl()` gets the right dashboard URL. New `WizardEntryPoint::setRequestContextOverride( ?string )` exposes the override slot; null clears it. The same admin-post-context issue affects every other wizard whose `submit()` returns a dashboard-relative `redirect_url` — the new-tournament wizard's redirect was on the same code path. After this fix, every wizard's "Create" CTA lands the user on the correct frontend dashboard URL. Patch bump — bug fix completing the #940 admin-post switch. (#940 follow-up) =

Multi-page if the range exceeds one page. Filter validation: `team_id` (required, > 0), `date_from` / `date_to` (Y-m-d, defaults: today → +28 days). **XLSX**: reuses the existing `team_activities` exporter (CSV exporter with `supportedFormats: ['csv', 'xlsx']` since v3.110.0) — no new backend code; the planner's button POSTs with `format=xlsx` against the same exporter key. Both buttons POST to `admin-post.php?action=tt_export` (the form-POST architecture from #939), so download headers fire cleanly and binary content is uncorrupted. Hidden fields: `tt_export_key`, `format`, `team_id`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `tt_export_return_url` — none of them are WP-reserved public query var names, so #940's Scan A passes; the URL is built via `admin_url('admin-post.php')` so #940's Scan B passes too. Buttons inherit the existing `.tt-btn .tt-btn-secondary` styling, each at 48px min-height so they meet the mobile-first tap-target floor; they wrap to a vertical stack below ~480px via the parent flex container's `flex-wrap`. Cap-gated on `tt_view_activities` at the exporter layer; the planner's own access check at view entry (`tt_view_plan`) gates the page that hosts the buttons. Out of scope: iCal subscription model (explicitly excluded), custom date-range picker on the planner (uses the planner's own range), multi-team bulk planning export (the central Exports page covers that), per-export branding picker (uses default brand-kit tokens), async export pipeline (sync is fine — max ~100 rows over a season). Patch bump — enhancement within the 4.3 minor (team planner already exists; this is an add-on, not a feature epic). (closes #947) =

= 4.3.17 — Exports XLSX downloads no longer corrupt; CSV downloads no longer prefixed with HTML chrome (closes #939, v4.2.2 #903 regression). The central exports surface (`?tt_view=exports`) emitted unusable files for every binary and text format since v4.2.2: XLSX downloads were corrupt (Excel refused to open them), CSV downloads contained the dashboard page HTML rather than CSV data, and JSON / ZIP / iCal downloads were similarly broken. Root cause was identical to the wizard 404 class (#940): the form-POST handler `FrontendExportsView::handleExportPost()` ran INSIDE the `[talenttrack_dashboard]` shortcode — i.e. after `wp_head()`, after the theme had streamed `<!DOCTYPE html>` + header + nav, and inside the shortcode's `ob_start()`. By the time the handler ran, response headers were already sent (so `header('Content-Type: application/...')` silently failed) and the binary/CSV bytes echoed into the shortcode's OB buffer, appended AFTER the page chrome the theme had streamed. The browser saved the whole HTML-plus-binary blob with the requested filename and `Content-Type: text/html`. Fix mirrors the #940 wizard switch: form POSTs now target `admin-post.php` with `action=tt_export`, handled by a new static method `FrontendExportsView::handleAdminPostExport()` registered on `admin_post_tt_export` in `ExportModule::boot()`. `admin-post.php` loads `wp-load.php` but does NOT bootstrap the theme, so download headers fire cleanly and bytes go straight onto the wire — XLSX is once again a valid ZIP from byte 0, CSV is once again CSV from byte 0. Errors carry back via a coded query param (`?tt_export_error=nonce|missing_key|unknown_key|service`) + a short-TTL transient (`tt_export_err_<uid>`) carrying the human-readable service-error message; `render()` resolves the code on the next GET and surfaces the same `tt-notice tt-notice--error` it always did above the export grid. `ExportRestController` (the REST route at `/wp-json/talenttrack/v1/exports/<key>`) stays unchanged — it bypasses the theme correctly and was always working; the form-POST surface is what was broken. `ScheduledReportsRunner` is unaffected (it calls `ExportService::run()` directly server-side, no HTTP layer). Patch bump — bug fix restoring every broken exporter format. (closes #939) =

= 4.3.16 — Wizard step-transition 404s + entry-link cleanup + CI lint gate (closes #940, supersedes #937). On the pilot install every step transition on the new-tournament wizard 404'd — same defect class lurked in new-team and team-blueprint. Root cause is architectural: `WP::parse_request()` reads public query vars from `\$_POST` **before** `\$_GET`. Three wizard step files emitted `<input type="text" name="name" required>`; the form had no `action=` attribute, so it POSTed `name=Den Helder` to the same URL → WP set `query_vars['name'] = 'Den Helder'`, tried to resolve a post with slug `den-helder`, found none, marked `is_404 = true`, and served the 404 template before `[talenttrack_dashboard]` could run. Three-layer fix. **Layer 1 (architectural)**: wizard form POSTs target `admin-post.php` (`action=tt_wizard_step`) instead of the current dashboard URL. `admin-post.php` loads `wp-load.php` but does NOT invoke `WP::main()` for the front-end template path, so the public-query-var resolution that 404'd the wizard doesn't run there. Forward-compatible against any future plugin registering a new public query var that happens to match a wizard field name. New handler `FrontendWizardView::handleAdminPostStep()` mirrors the legacy POST branch (verify nonce → dispatch on `tt_wizard_action` → persist → redirect); `render()` is now GET-only. Hidden field `tt_wizard_return_url` carries the wizard URL through admin-post.php so the handler can redirect back; transient `tt_wizard_err_*` carries validation errors back so the next GET surfaces them visibly. Hook registered in `WizardsModule::boot()` as `admin_post_tt_wizard_step` (no `admin_post_nopriv` — every wizard requires login). **Layer 2 (subsumes #937)**: the 5 surviving direct `slug=` URL writes migrate to `WizardEntryPoint::buildUrl()`: `FrontendTeamBlueprintsView` (new-team-blueprint button), `FrontendMatchPrepView` (match-prep redirect), `FrontendActivitiesManageView` (Continue rating link), `ParentSearchPickerComponent` (new-person inline create), `OnboardingPage` (new-team button). `WizardEntryPoint::urlFor()` gains a third `\$extra_args` parameter; new sibling `WizardEntryPoint::buildUrl()` is the caller-friendly variant for when there's no flat-form fallback URL to hand. **Layer 3 (regression prevention)**: new CI workflow `.github/workflows/wizard-form-lint.yml`. Scan A fails the build if any `*Step.php` under `src/Modules/Wizards/`, `src/Modules/Tournaments/Wizard/`, `src/Modules/MatchPrep/Wizards/`, `src/Modules/Vct/Wizard/` declares an `<input|select|textarea>` named after any of ~25 WP-reserved public query vars. Scan B fails the build if any file outside the allow-list (the helper itself, `FrontendWizardView`, `MfaLoginGuard`) builds a wizard URL via `add_query_arg(['tt_view'=>'wizard',…])`. **Field renames** (defensive, even though Layer 1 makes them strictly unnecessary): `BasicsStep::name` → `tournament_name`, `BasicsStep::name` (team) → `team_name`, `SetupStep::name` (blueprint) → `blueprint_name`. State keys (`'name'`) unchanged so downstream `submit()` / repository writes don't change. Patch bump — bug fix restoring three broken wizards + architectural-class regression prevention. (closes #940, supersedes #937) =

= 4.3.15 — Team planner calendar day-header shows correct localised day abbreviations on non-English installs (closes #945). On a Dutch install the team planner's calendar showed the literal letter `V` in every column header instead of `ma di wo do vr za zo`. Root cause: [`FrontendTeamPlannerView.php:222`](src/Modules/Planning/Frontend/FrontendTeamPlannerView.php#L222) called `wp_date( __( 'D', 'talenttrack' ), … )` — wrapping a PHP date-format character through `__()`. The Dutch `.po` carried `msgid "D" msgstr "V"` because the matrix admin page legitimately uses `__( 'D' )` for the column abbreviation for "Verwijderen" (Delete). gettext doesn't distinguish the two uses — same `msgid`, both call sites resolved to `msgstr "V"`. The planner then got `wp_date('V', …)` and emitted the literal `'V'` because that's not a recognised date-format character. Three fixes: (1) `FrontendTeamPlannerView.php:222-223` — drop the `__()` wrapping on `'D'` and `'M j'`; `wp_date()` already localises its output through the site locale. (2) `MatrixPage.php:47-49` — disambiguate the matrix column abbreviations via `_x( 'R'|'C'|'D', 'matrix column abbreviation for Read|Change|Delete', 'talenttrack' )` so future date-format `'D'` calls don't collide with the matrix's Delete column. (3) `languages/talenttrack-nl_NL.po` — replace the un-contextualised matrix entries with the new `msgctxt`-aware ones (`msgstr "L"` for Read → Lezen, `"A"` for Change → Aanpassen, `"V"` for Delete → Verwijderen); the `i18n-sync` workflow regenerates the .pot and msgmerges the other locale .po files on push to main. After this fix the planner emits `ma di wo do vr za zo` on Dutch (and locale-correct equivalents on fr/de/es), and the matrix admin keeps its localised single-letter abbreviations. No behavioural change for English-locale installs. Patch bump — UI fix. (closes #945) =

= 4.3.14 — Match Prep + Match Execution critical-error fix (closes #955). Both `?tt_view=match-prep` and `?tt_view=match-execution` surfaces fataled with a generic "There has been a critical error on this website" page on first load. Root cause: PHP visibility narrowing — `FrontendMatchPrepView` and `FrontendMatchExecutionView` extend `FrontendViewBase` (whose `enqueueAssets()` is `protected static`) but redeclared the method as `private static`, which PHP rejects at class-load time. `FrontendMatchExecutionView`'s override additionally widened the signature (`(int $activity_id, ?object $execution): void`), making the override a double-fault — either alone is fatal. Fix renames each view's local method to `enqueueViewAssets()` (with the per-view signature it already had) and calls `parent::enqueueAssets()` first inside `render()` so the shared chrome assets (`tt-frontend-mobile.css`, `tt-table-tools.js`, `tt-frontend-archive-button.js`) load alongside the per-view scoped enqueues. Parent's idempotency guard (`self::\$assets_enqueued`) prevents double-enqueue. No schema, no migration, no REST contract change; class-load fatal goes away, the rest of `render()` was always correct. Patch bump — bug fix restoring two broken surfaces. (closes #955) =

= 4.3.8 — `Lookup translation lint` CI gate goes green; non-English locales see localised status/priority labels everywhere (closes #923). The architectural endgame (push `LookupTranslator` into the repository SELECT layer so view code can't bypass by construction) stays in #806's tech-debt queue.
